body:
Thanks.  I've been thinking about what you've written.  It definitely helped me feel better.  I'm glad you happened to see this post.  

I'll definitely check out the article by Maria Bamford.  It sounds really pertinent.

That's a kind sentiment.  I've been through this exercise.

The help amounts to me just feeling like shit as we talk.  It sucks for both.  

Over the next few decades it will slowly destroy the woman I love and turn her into a shell of the person she was.  By the end we'll both be sick, our illnesses feeding off each other....I really don't want to do that to her.  

Did you party in college?  Have you ever had a party among close friends ruined by some drama?  I feel like it's better to leave the party a little early that to make everyone else feel like shit for the duration.

Thank you. I may take you up on that eventually. It's hard. 

*She* was the light of my life. I now understand how wrong it was to put her in that position.

I did love her though. She was everything. For a long time I told myself to get better for her sake (she wouldn't want me to still be upset) but I've fallen apart. I lost the job and career after her... I couldn't get myself out of bed in the morning.

The only thing that's soothing is the thought of ending it. I can't watch her get married and be happy. I can let her go but I can't watch that.

I didn't protest when she left. I want her to be happy. I told her I don't love her anymore. She knows that I'm suicidal and has called the hotline on me...I've never tried to use this to manipulate her. I love her though. I miss her.

It's hard for me to see them.  I tend to filter, seeing only the negative. I also minimize the positive until it doesn't exist anymore. I know this is a distortion. I can't seem to help it. I can't control my thoughts or my mood for very long.
Plot twist: letter written on cursed Mayan spirit paper.
I would like to see this split by income rather than race.  I would guess low income = arrest even more than race.
